weather_reasons: NWS hourly forecast includes thunderstorm potential
Phoenix NWS discussion contains a convective/monsoon signal

afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 241246
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
546 AM MST Thu Sep 24 2026

.UPDATE...13Z Aviation Discussion

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Scattered showers and thunderstorms will be possible again this 
  afternoon and evening, with activity mainly focused over the 
  foothills and high terrain features.

- After drying out temporarily this weekend, rain chances will return
  to the region late Sunday into Monday as tropical moisture gets
  pulled northward into the Desert Southwest.

- Near to slightly above normal temperatures will persist through
  the weekend before noticeably cooling early next week.
 
&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Friday/... 
Storm coverage was much lower than high-res models indicated last
night which was mainly due to lower instability and a stronger 
cap in place from extensive cloud cover over southcentral AZ. 
Latest wv satellite imagery and area radars still show abundant 
high clouds streaming into AZ with showers and thunderstorms 
percolating over southern portions of the state. All of this 
activity is developing ahead of a coastal low pressure system 
located west of the Baja California (not related to the hurricanes
much farther south). As we head through this morning, several 
lobes of vorticity will progress northward out of MX and provide a
focus of lift for additional showers and storms this afternoon 
into this evening. 

It is difficult to pinpoint exactly where these vortmaxes will end 
up moving as some models focus convective activity over the western 
deserts this afternoon while others bring storms into central AZ. 
Either way, there will likely be another round of widely scattered 
convection this afternoon, especially over the terrain features of 
southwest AZ and the foothills and higher terrain areas NE of 
Phoenix. There is still around a 20-30% chance that storms form over 
the lower deserts, but this will be highly dependent on if activity 
across the higher terrain can congeal enough to produce strong 
outflows which could generate additional convection. Instability 
will not be as high as yesterday (SBCAPE < 1000 J/kg) but there 
still could be a strong storm or two which could produce locally 
gusty winds and patchy blowing dust. The coastal low will weaken 
and lift northward on Friday which will cause upper-lvl winds to 
shift out of the west and bring much drier air into our region. 
Coincidentally, PoPs will decrease below 10% across the entire 
region on Friday.

The presence of the upper-low over the next couple of days promoting 
near seasonal 500 mb hghts, coupled with periods of extensive high
clouds will help keep temperatures near normal across southcentral
AZ. Highs across the lower deserts of central AZ will likely 
remain in the mid to upper 90s both today and Friday. Temperatures
along and west of the Colorado River valley will be slightly 
warmer with highs reaching the lower 100s. Overall, the HeatRisk 
should remain in the minor category with only very small pockets 
of moderate. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Saturday through Wednesday/... 
Dry westerly flow is expected to persist through at least 
Saturday with large scale troughing remaining over the Pac NW 
while the subtropical ridge slowly shifts southwestward from east 
TX into the interior of MX. Due to the presence of the ridge to 
our east, 500 mb hghts are expected to peak around 586-588 dam 
Saturday afternoon. This will result in highs topping out between 
100-105 degrees across the lower deserts (4-6 degrees above 
normal) under mostly sunny skies and zero chance of rain. From 
Sunday into early next week, there does look to be a significant 
degree of cooling as tropical moisture arrives and rain chances 
increase. Highs will likely fall below 100 degrees across the 
lower deserts on Sunday and continue to cool to the upper 80s and 
lower 90s Monday through Wednesday.

Our attention then turns to the tropical Pacific Sunday into early 
next week where potential moisture from two weakening hurricanes 
(Polo and Odalys) will come into play. There is still a high degree 
of uncertainty as to a) how far north the residual moisture will be 
shed out ahead of these decaying storms, and b) where the plume(s) 
of moisture will set up. Another major question mark will be just 
how deep and progressive a developing trough of low pressure will be 
over the Intermountain West. All of these factors will have to line 
up perfectly for our forecast area to get significant rainfall. 
Both the GEFS and EPS are telling a different story with varying 
degrees of moisture and timing and intensity of said trough which 
is really complicating things. The latest NHC track for Hurricane
Polo shows the storm making landfall along the coast of the Baja 
California by Monday which if aligned with the passage of the 
aforementioned trough would draw a large plume of moisture into 
interior MX and and much of AZ. NBM PoPs have already increased to
around 20-30% with an initial band of moisture on Sunday, but 
with the main lift arriving on Monday, PoPs are now widespread 
30-60% across our forecast area. The remnant tropical moisture may
linger into Tuesday before fully exiting the region on Wednesday.
It is also worth pointing out that some ensemble members are 
showing significant rainfall totals in excess of 1-2" across 
southcentral AZ Monday-Tuesday but there is still significant 
spread between members. Therefore, we will likely have to wait 
until this weekend for things to become more clear. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1245Z. 

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 

Showers and thunderstorms during the pre-dawn and dawn hours have
popped up across portions of the region but were not captured 
well in prior forecast guidance. Due to very low forecast 
confidence, metro TAFs may need to be updated for the next few 
hours until convection begins to diminish. Sudden wind shifts and
perhaps some brief reductions in surface VIS will be the main
operation concerns.

Another round of SHRA/TSRA are possible later today, but overall 
forecast confidence in this potential and timing is low. Isolated
to scattered showers may develop in/move into the metro from the 
south later Thursday morning/midday. This is reflected with VCSH 
in the TAFs in the morning. SHRA/TSRA may then develop in the 
metro later in the afternoon-evening timeframe, but chances will 
be higher outside the metro area. Activity around the region will 
be capable of producing several outflow boundaries which may cause
erratic wind behavior and outflow collisions could lead to new 
development. Winds tonight through Thursday morning will continue 
to favor an E/SE component with light speeds. Confidence in winds 
then degrades from there with winds potentially influenced by 
showers and/or cloud cover through the afternoon and evening. 
Thick high cirrus cigs and brief periods of cigs as low as 8-10K 
ft AGL will continue through the TAF period. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 

There is a low chance (10%) for VCTS/TS at KBLH Thursday
afternoon. Otherwise, no weather issues are expected through
Thursday evening under increasing high cirrus decks. Confidence 
in a specific wind direction at any given time is low given the 
weak pressure gradient. Extended periods of light and variable 
winds will be common. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Widely scattered showers and thunderstorms will be possible again
this afternoon and early evening, mainly focused over the higher
terrain of the eastern districts. Localized gusty and erratic 
winds will be possible in the vicinity of any storm that develops.
Rain chances will decrease Friday into this weekend before much 
better chances for wetting rainfall arrives early next week. 
MinRHs will range from 25-35% today with a gradual decrease to 
around 15-25% on region-wide Saturday. Significant moisture return
is expected across the eastern districts by Monday which will 
keep RH values above 40% with excellent overnight recovery. Winds 
will generally follow diurnal patterns with speeds around 10-15 
mph with typical afternoon gusts in the upper teens.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Salerno
LONG TERM...Salerno
AVIATION...Benedict/18/RW 
FIRE WEATHER...Salerno
